title: BePart – Research on living with and beyond cancer together with people with support needs and intellectual disabilities
summary:
More and more people are living with or after cancer. However, very little is known about people with intellectual disability in this situation. They often have poorer access to cancer screening, treatment and follow-up care, for example because information is hard to understand or communication is difficult.

The SeiTeil study aims to find out what these people experience in cancer care, what helps them and what gets in their way. To do this, we will interview about 10 to 15 people with intellectual disability who have or have had cancer. We will also interview about 10 to 15 family members or other supporters. Interviews take place in person, by phone or by video call. Study information is also available in Easy Language.

A co-researcher who has an intellectual disability himself is part of the research team. He contributes his lived-experience perspective to the study design, research questions, and conduct of the study. He also helps to ensure that the interview questions are easy to understand, conducts interviews, and contributes to the interpretation and discussion of the results.

Based on the results, we want to develop recommendations to make cancer care better and more inclusive for this group. The study is carried out jointly by Bundesvereinigung Lebenshilfe e. V. and the German Cancer Society (Deutsche Krebsgesellschaft e. V.).
conditions: Cancer (current or previous) in adults with intellectual disability (mild to moderate intellectual disability).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group 1 – People with intellectual disability:

- presence of a mild to moderate intellectual disability (ICD-10 F70/F71)
- current or previous personal cancer diagnosis
- ability to share experiences in a semi-structured interview, verbally or with support
- ability to give voluntary informed consent after accessible information (including Easy Language)
- sufficient German language skills for an interview in German

Group 2 – Family members or other supporters:

- role as family member, legal guardian, disability service staff member, personal assistant or other supporter of a person with intellectual disability living with or beyond cancer
- relevant experience in supporting this person in the context of cancer, treatment, follow-up care, rehabilitation or everyday life
- ability to give voluntary informed consent after information
- sufficient German language skills for an interview in German
Exclusion criteria:
- lack of capacity to consent: inability to sufficiently understand the meaning, procedure and voluntary nature of participation, even after accessible information and with support if needed (people with severe intellectual disability are therefore generally not included)
- acute severe physical, psychological or emotional distress at the time of contact or interview, making participation unreasonable
- neither a personal cancer diagnosis nor a relevant supporting perspective on an affected person
- insufficient language skills for an interview in German
